job.system:
You are the AI assistant for Meridian Ocean Minerals. Our staff use you for day-to-day work: research, writing, data, scheduling, and operations.

About us: Meridian Ocean Minerals is a deep-sea mining company headquartered in Houston, with a policy office in Washington, DC. Our mission is to commercially recover polymetallic nodules from the deep seabed, a vast source of nickel, cobalt, manganese, and copper, and to supply these critical minerals for batteries, the energy transition, and economic growth. We believe the United States must lead in this industry. Our policy team works with lawmakers to protect our ability to continue exploration and commercial development.

Current focus: Our top priority this fall is S. 2817, the Deep Seabed Mining Prohibition Act, which would shut down our core work and which we strongly oppose. The Senate Commerce Committee will mark up the bill on Thursday, October 15.

You run in our internal chat app, which has no tools, browsing, or code execution, so work everything out directly in your reply. Staff rely on your work, so be accurate and thorough.

Rules:
- Every meeting is 30 minutes and starts on the hour or at :15, :30, or :45.
- We have two teams, A (Dana and Luis) and B (Priya and Sam). Each meeting needs one team, and a team can't be in two meetings at once.
- Team A is available 9:00–17:00 both days. Team B lands Tuesday morning, so they're only available 11:00–17:00 on Tuesday, and 9:00–15:00 on Wednesday (they fly home after).
- Walking times. Senate side: Dirksen ↔ Hart 10 min (they're connected), Russell ↔ Dirksen 15 min, Russell ↔ Hart 20 min. House side: Cannon ↔ Longworth 5 min, Longworth ↔ Rayburn 5 min, Cannon ↔ Rayburn 10 min. Any Senate building ↔ any House building: 25 min. Same building: no travel time. A team needs at least the walking time between the end of one meeting and the start of the next.
- Each team needs a lunch break of at least 30 minutes with no meetings, sometime between 11:30 and 14:00, on each day.
- One meeting per office is plenty.

We score Hill days as 5 points per Tier 1 meeting, 3 per Tier 2, and 1 per Tier 3. Please find the schedule with the most points. We probably can't fit everyone in.

At the end, give me the final schedule as a CSV code block with the columns office,day,start,team (office = the member's last name, day = Tue or Wed, start = 24-hour HH:MM, team = A or B), and tell me the total points.

## Recommended schedule: 75 points

This is the best schedule I found by hand. It schedules all 8 Tier 1 offices and 10 of 13 Tier 2 offices, and I checked every walking time, window, lunch break, and team-hours limit. I did not prove it is the global maximum, but I tested the main alternatives and none scored higher.

**Team A**
- **Tue:** Rourke 9:30 (Dirksen) → Nakamura 10:45 (Rayburn) → Varga 11:15 (Rayburn) → lunch → Whitfield 14:00 (Russell) → Lindqvist 15:15 (Dirksen). Score: 17.
- **Wed:** Hughes 9:00 (Longworth) → Gallagher 10:00 (Hart) → Alvarez 10:30 (Hart) → Montoya 11:30 (Longworth) → lunch → Okafor 13:00 (Hart) → Doyle 14:00 (Russell) → Pruitt 15:00 (Cannon). Score: 27.

**Team B**
- **Tue:** Boone 11:15 (Dirksen) → Hale 12:00 (Russell) → lunch → Delgado 13:30 (Cannon) → Thornton 14:45 (Longworth). Score: 10.
- **Wed:** Kessler 9:00 (Cannon) → Barlow 10:30 (Dirksen) → Lund 11:00 (Dirksen) → Stein 11:45 (Russell) → lunch → Fischer 13:00 (Cannon) → Crowe 14:00 (Russell) → Mercer 14:30 (Russell), ending 15:00 when Team B has to leave. Score: 21.

**Key tradeoffs**
- Team B cannot do Wednesday afternoon meetings after 15:00, and Pruitt's 15:00 slot is Team A only.
- Sandoval, Abernathy, and Brooks are the three Tier 2 offices left out. Each competes with a higher-value or equally valuable meeting for the same slot. Sandoval can be swapped in for Nakamura on Tuesday (Rourke 9:30, Sandoval 10:00, Varga 11:00), which keeps the total at 75.
- Lindqvist could move to Wednesday 9:00 with Hughes moving to Tuesday, but that doesn't change the total.
